values.description: The past observations of the target series, oldest first; null marks a missing observation. At most 32768 (the trained context), with at least one number.

horizon.description: How many future steps to forecast, from 1 to 4096. Up to 1024 steps come from one pass; longer horizons are forecast in blocks of 1024, each block's median appended to the context, as the maker does.

quantile_levels.description: Which of the 21 trained quantile levels to return, unique, in any order (the reply lists them ascending). Defaults to all 21.

co_targets.description: Further target series over the same past steps as values (same length, null for missing), forecast jointly with it: the maker's multivariate forecasting. Their forecasts come back in co_target_forecasts. The reply holds at most 640,000 forecast numbers: (1 + co_targets) x horizon x (levels + 1).

past_covariates.description: Numeric covariates known only over the past (same length as values, null for missing). The model reads them but does not forecast them. A value beyond the float32 range counts as missing.

covariates.description: Numeric known-future covariates (calendar features, planned events, prices, weather forecasts): each spans the past and the horizon, len(values) + horizon steps, null for missing. A value beyond the float32 range counts as missing.

categorical_past_covariates.description: Categorical covariates known only over the past, as category codes (any numbers; null is its own category), same length as values. They are target-encoded against the target's history, as the maker does; with co_targets the codes are used as they are.

categorical_covariates.description: Categorical known-future covariates as category codes over len(values) + horizon steps. A code first seen in the horizon resolves to the series mean.

symmetric_averaging.description: Average with the mirrored forecast of the negated series and covariates (runs the model twice), the maker's default. Default true.

clip_nonnegative.description: Clip a forecast at zero when that series' observed history is non-negative, the maker's default. Default true.
